scenes.tts: A tree with no leaves in winter is not dead. It is resting. Visit one tree all year, watch the seasons come in the same order, and find the buds already holding next spring's leaves.
scenes.narration: A tree with no leaves in winter is not dead. It is resting. Visit one tree all year, watch the seasons come in the same order, and find the buds already holding next spring's leaves.

items.text: Seasons come in the same order

scenes.tts: You need one tree that loses its leaves in fall, one you can reach safely and have permission to visit. Bring a phone or camera and paper.

items.text: Tree that loses leaves in fall

scenes.narration: You need one tree that loses its leaves in fall, one you can reach safely and have permission to visit. Bring a phone or camera and paper.

scenes.tts: Stand ten to twenty steps back, so the whole tree fits in the photo. Pick a landmark, and take every photo from there, facing the same way. Your child predicts first.
scenes.narration: Stand ten to twenty steps back, so the whole tree fits in the photo. Pick a landmark, and take every photo from there, facing the same way. Your child predicts first.

scenes.tts: Visit about once a month for fifteen minutes. Notice the weather and look for animals. In much of Virginia, buds swell and open in March and April. Dates vary. Compare each new photo with the last one. A bare winter twig still has buds, so the tree is resting, not dead.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child at the tree on every visit. Feet stay on the ground, with no climbing, and nothing from the tree goes in a mouth.

scenes.line: A bare tree in winter is resting, not dead.
